## Description

A small pear-shaped ciliate (40–60 × 20–30 µm) that filters bacteria with a mouth of membranelles:
the laboratory ciliate par excellence and the prey with which the growth of *Amoeba* is measured. It
swims at ~500 µm/s. It is amicronucleate (no micronucleus), so it does not conjugate (*T. thermophila*
does). It has mucocysts, not trichocysts. It grows best at ~27 °C.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 10 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A filter feeder with helical swimming; what it releases into the water (the "stomatin": ferrous iron,
hypoxanthine, uracil) is a [released signal](../../mechanics/chemical-signals.md) that turns *T. vorax* into a
macrostome (rate and half-life estimated; small-molecule diffusion).
